artworks.title: Daedalus and Icarus
artworks.description: Van Dyck shows the father fastening wax and feathers — the warning spoken before the boy climbed too close to the sun.

artworks.title: Landscape with the Fall of Icarus
artworks.description: A ploughman keeps his furrow and a galleon sails on while two white legs vanish into the green sea — the fall reduced to a splash nobody notices. Long attributed to Bruegel and now generally thought an early copy of his lost original, the painting in Brussels inspired Auden's Musée des Beaux Arts.

artworks.title: The Lament for Icarus
artworks.description: Fallen Icarus lies among mourning nymphs, his great wings still spread — Tate Britain's Victorian elegy for the boy who flew too high, the myth retold as romantic martyrdom rather than unnoticed splash.

artworks.title: The Fall of Icarus
artworks.artist: Jacob Peter Gowy (after Peter Paul Rubens)
artworks.description: Prado oil after Rubens for the Torre de la Parada: Daedalus still climbs while Icarus plunges headlong, wax and feathers scattering — the Baroque fall as pure kinetic catastrophe.

artworks.title: Landscape with the Fall of Icarus
artworks.description: Stockholm Nationalmuseum's Flemish panorama nearly loses the boy in the vista — travellers and peaks keep moving while one winged figure falls, the Bruegel lesson restaged as mountain theatre.

music.title: Flight of Icarus
music.description: Maiden's single from Piece of Mind, cut while the wax myth was pure heavy-metal material: the boy's climb becomes a son's defiance of a betraying father, and the fall a blaze of glory rather than a warning heeded.

popCulture.title: Musée des Beaux Arts
popCulture.creator: W. H. Auden
popCulture.description: Auden's poem, written after standing before Bruegel's Fall of Icarus in Brussels, reads the unnoticed splash as the shape of all suffering — the ploughman keeps his furrow, the ship sails calmly on, and disaster happens off to the side.

popCulture.title: Kid Icarus
popCulture.creator: Nintendo
popCulture.description: Pit, a winged boy archer, escapes an underworld prison to save a Greek-flavoured skyworld from Medusa. The name and the wings are Icarus' own — borrowed for a flight that, for once, ends happily.
